question:
What would you
build from nothing?
next_voice: Next, in Part Five: the daughters.

beats.text: The governor gave her a stable.
In 1658, Maisonneuve gave her an old stone stable.
beats.scene: An old seventeenth-century stone stable with a low sagging roof and a plain wooden door standing half open, on the edge of a small colonial town in snow at dusk, a lantern glowing in the dark doorway, hard side light, mist. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: She turned it into a school.
It was the first school in Montreal.
She taught the children of the colony.
beats.scene: Seen only from behind: rows of small children in plain dark seventeenth-century clothes sitting on bare wooden benches in a rough stone room, facing a tall window that throws a hard shaft of light across the floor, dust drifting, a slate on the far wall. No faces visible, backs of heads only.

beats.text: Years after she crossed the ocean, her work had begun.
The Vatican biography says she also saw to the restoring of the cross on Mount Royal.
beats.scene: A tall plain wooden cross standing on the summit of a wooded mountain at dusk above a wide river valley and a tiny fort-town far below, hard low light from one side, mist in the valley, vast dark forest. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: But a school was only the beginning.
